newsitem.title: USA: Late U.S. cash products hold gains following NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: Late U.S. cash products hold gains following NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices remained at signinficantly higher levels in late afternoon dealings on Tuesday, still lifted by military action in Iraq and the U.N.'s postponement of its oil-for-food agreement.
Most grades of gasoline and distillates rose to 1.50 to 2.50 cents a gallon higher than late Thursday's levels, off significantly from the early morning highs, but up from the session lows.
The market jumped higher on news the U.S. fired long range cruise-missles at Iraqi targets in southern Iraq in response for Iraq's attack on Kurds there.

As expected, the United Nations postponed the oil-for-food plan in reaction to Iraq's military actions. The deal, which seemed very close to total ratification just a few weeks ago, clould be delayed for "some time," a U.S. State Department official said on Tuesday.
Cash market trade was much less exciting, traders said. Differentials were generally static as players returned from the long holiday weekend and assessed positions.
Most gasoline and distillate values were stable to narrowly higher than levels seen last week. Jet fuel offers at both centers firmed on the military news, traders said.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
